references.name: den-oever-2013
references.author: MD van Leeuwen
references.observed: Ordinary2013 aerial inspected: three separate banks of gate/pier structures along the Den Oever causeway,roadway continuing across the gate rows,a separate navigable lock with long open approach channel and swing bridge,low service buildings and grass islands/armored sloping shorelines. Wind turbine,boats,people and vehicles are independent. Dated image predates current major pumping works;do not infer a current complete2026 complex from this alone. Keep waterway openings physically open.

references.name: causeway-section
references.use: Ordinary image reference only;not a texture and not redistributed.
references.observed: Ordinary aerial cross-section inspected: two separate motorway carriageways,parallel path,wide sloping grass embankment and armored seaward toe,rest area/harbor projections. Preserve both sea and lake water;do not model the causeway as a bridge deck in open water. Vehicles,boats,wind turbines and signage remain independent.

references.name: den-oever-works
references.use: Ordinary image reference only;not a texture and not redistributed.
references.observed: Ordinary2024 works aerial inspected: the legacy Den Oever sluice rows remain,with major adjacent pumping/flow-channel construction and altered shore pads. Separate open navigation lock and approach basin remain visible. This image prevents treating the2013 photograph as current complete geometry;unseen2026 construction must remain explicitly uncertain. Not a survey or a texture.

references.name: kornwerderzand-aerial
references.use: Ordinary picture reference only;not redistributed as a texture.
references.observed: Ordinary aerial inspected: two distinct five-bay sluice banks west of a separate road/navigation crossing,two parallel navigation-lock chambers farther southeast,long open harbor approaches,armored grassy banks and low independent harbor/service buildings. Static closed road bridge is visible. Exact chamber dimensions and current redevelopment are not surveyed.
